name: Comp AI
description: Open-source-friendly compliance SaaS that automates evidence collection, policy generation, and continuous monitoring for SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, and GDPR. Sold to startups through enterprise as "compliance that helps you close deals." Founded Jan 2025, US. ~1,000 estimated users on TrustMRR.

mentions.evidence: ~$11,911 MRR, 49 active subscriptions, ~$697,350–$699,725 L30, ~$5,791,980 all-time. Last sync Oct 4, 2026 ~05:33 Warsaw (03:33 UTC).
mentions.indieAngle: Own one compliance framework wedge (SOC 2 Type II evidence, or ISO 27001 for EU SMBs, or HIPAA for clinics) with annual seats + audit-week setup packs. Sell to the person who has to close the security questionnaire.

mentions.evidence: MRR $14,628, 57 subscriptions. Last 30 days $738,807. All-time $6,343,999. About 1,000 users, company-stated. Revenue synced 27 October 2026 ~04:25 Warsaw. The 4 October note was about $11,911 a month, 49 subscriptions, about $700,000 in the last 30 days, and about $5.8 million all-time.
mentions.indieAngle: One audit a buyer already asks for, with a setup fee and a smaller watch fee after.

whyItPrints: Security-questionnaire and audit bureaucracy glue. Once policies and evidence live in Comp AI, switching is painful, and the renewal is part of selling to another company. The monthly subscriptions are the smaller line. The last 30 days are much larger, which fits annual contracts and setup fees.
whyThisMatters:
Startups use Comp AI when a customer asks for security paperwork. You pick SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, GDPR, or FedRAMP. It drafts the policies, pulls evidence from tools you already use, and flags gaps. They say there are more than 580 integrations, and that an audit and a pentest come with it.

A person answers in Slack. They say the reply is under three minutes. You can send a prospect a trust page.

Daniel Rascon at Persona AI describes leaving Vanta and starting a SOC 2 observation period in under two weeks. The site links a TechCrunch story about a Series A. The listing dates the company to January 2025.

The 4 October note had forty-nine subscriptions. This one has fifty-seven. The last 30 days are still many times the monthly subscriptions, same shape as before.
